input: Learn to read a wine label properly

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Wine labels differ significantly between Old World (European) and New World (e.g. US, Australian) wines — knowing which to focus on determines what label elements to teach (region vs. grape variety, classification systems, etc.)
Whether this is for personal use, to impress at social events, or for a professional context (e.g. hospitality work) changes the depth and focus of what needs to be learned.
The setting — buying wine in a shop, reading a restaurant menu, or collecting — changes which label elements matter most (price tier, vintage, producer, appellation, etc.)
How much time the user can dedicate shapes whether this is a quick overview or a deep study plan with structured resources.
Some people learn best through visual guides, others through books, videos, or hands-on tasting — the preferred learning style determines what resources and methods to recommend.
Knowing what 'done well' looks like — e.g. confidently choosing a bottle, passing a quiz, explaining a label to others — sets a clear target and stopping point for the plan.
Whether the user wants a self-study plan, a course, an app, or a structured cheat-sheet determines the immediate next action and format of the output.

gold.taskTitle: Learn to read a wine label properly
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to understand how to interpret the information on a wine label correctly and confidently.

questions.title: Which wine region styles are you focusing on?
questions.description: Old World labels (France, Italy, Spain) use region-based naming, while New World labels (USA, Australia, Argentina) typically name the grape variety. Knowing the focus shapes which label conventions to prioritise.

questions.title: What is your main reason for learning this?
questions.description: Understanding whether this is for personal enjoyment, social confidence, a job in hospitality, or something else determines how technical and detailed the plan needs to be.

questions.title: Where will you most often be reading labels?
questions.description: A shop, a restaurant wine list, a cellar, or online retail each foreground different label elements — price tier, vintage, appellation, alcohol content, etc.

questions.title: How much time can you commit to learning this?
questions.description: A single evening overview vs. a multi-week structured study plan requires very different approaches and resource recommendations.

questions.title: How do you prefer to absorb new knowledge?
questions.description: Videos, illustrated guides, written articles, flashcard apps, or hands-on tasting sessions each suit different learners — this determines which resources to recommend.

questions.title: What would confident label-reading look like for you?
questions.description: For example: choosing a bottle unaided, explaining a label to a friend, never feeling confused in a shop — having a clear success image defines when the goal is achieved.

questions.title: Do you want a study plan, a cheat sheet, or a course?
questions.description: The preferred format — a step-by-step learning plan, a single reference document, an app, or a formal course recommendation — determines the immediate next action.
